Calamity

/kuh-LAM-ih-tee/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Calamity means an event that causes great and often sudden damage or distress; a disaster

The wildfire that swept through the foothill town of Pine Ridge was a calamity no one had prepared for, reducing three hundred homes to ash in a single afternoon.

Worked Example

When the fishing fleet was caught in a sudden ice storm off the northern coast, the calamity cost the village nearly half its boats and left dozens of families without their livelihood.

The storm strikes suddenly and causes enormous damage and distress: boats destroyed and livelihoods lost. That combination of sudden, serious, widespread harm is exactly what makes an event a calamity rather than a minor setback.

How Calamity Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

disaster

disaster: an event causing great harm or loss

catastrophe

catastrophe: a sudden, large-scale disaster

tragedy

tragedy: a deeply sad and destructive event

Antonyms

blessing

blessing: something that brings good fortune

windfall

windfall: an unexpected piece of good luck

How Strong Is It? — mishap → calamity → cataclysm

mishap vs. calamity

mishap vs. calamity: A mishap is a small accident, like spilling paint on the floor, while a calamity causes serious, widespread damage and distress.

cataclysm vs. calamity

cataclysm vs. calamity: A calamity devastates a town or a community, but a cataclysm is even bigger: a violent upheaval that can reshape an entire region or society.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — calam-

Root — calam-: from Latin calamitas, meaning damage, loss, or disaster

Suffix — -ity

Suffix — -ity: forms nouns naming a state or condition

Put it together

Put it together: The Latin root calam- carries the idea of damage and ruin, and the noun suffix -ity turns it into a thing you can name: a calamity, an actual event of great damage.

Use the root in a new word: calamitous

Use the root in a new word: calamitous: The report described the calamitous effects of the prolonged drought on the region's cattle herds.
